headline: Macao hold swings hurt profit; buybacks ramp up
summary_short: Net revenue was roughly flat at $3,154M (-0.7% y/y) as unusually low hold in Macao's rolling play offset volume growth, while net income attributable to LVS fell 24.9% y/y to $346M ($0.53 diluted EPS) on a higher effective tax rate and softer Macao EBITDA margins.
summary_long: Consolidated adjusted property EBITDA fell 16.1% y/y to $1,119M as unusually low rolling-chip hold across Macao properties -- The Venetian Macao's win rate ran 0.62% versus an expected 3.3% -- offset higher table-games and slot volumes. Macao segment EBITDA fell 24% y/y to $430M despite that volume growth. Marina Bay Sands' EBITDA margin also compressed 5.4pts to 49.9% on lower revenue. The effective tax rate rose to 19.1% from 14.8%, driven by Singapore's 17% statutory rate. LVS repurchased $787M of stock in the quarter, and its board lifted the buyback authorization to $6.0B; unrestricted cash was $3.38B after collecting $1.26B from the Las Vegas seller-financing loan repayment. No forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: CEO Patrick Dumont said Macao volumes grew across gaming segments but "unusually low hold in rolling play negatively impacted our reported financial results"; Marina Bay Sands delivered "industry-leading financial performance."
Macao segment EBITDA fell 24% y/y to $430M as rolling-chip win rates ran well below expectations across properties (e.g. Venetian 0.62% vs. 3.3% expected), despite higher table and slot volumes.
Effective tax rate rose to 19.1% from 14.8%, primarily driven by a 17% statutory rate on Singapore operations, compounding the operating-profit decline from weak Macao hold.
Macao volumes grew across gaming segments, but revenue was held back by unusually low rolling-chip hold in Macao casino play, largely offsetting that volume growth and Marina Bay Sands' scale.
